extracted.intended_audience: NIH R21 applicants and NIH peer reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: A Summary Statement / peer review critique for an NIH R21 application describing the review criteria, numeric scores for Significance/Investigator/Innovation/Approach/Environment, and additional review considerations (human subjects, animals, biohazards, select agents, resource sharing, budget).

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the project addresses an important problem or a critical barrier to progress in the field and the potential to improve scientific knowledge, technical capability, and/or clinical practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers' comments: 'Burkholderia pseudomallei is a poorly understood emerging pathogen... this study provides a straightforward analysis of its pathogenesis.' Strengths cited: 'Enteric infection seems a likely route of pathogenesis'; 'The work has the potential to transform our understanding of the pathogenesis of melioidosis'; 'The discovery indicates that there is a significant oral route of infection, and has the potential to significantly expand our understanding.' Weakness/consideration: 'How much of the pathology due to inhalation is due to ingestion?' (questioning the relative importance of the proposed route). Numeric example scores in critiques: 1–2 (lower is better).

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the appropriateness of the PD/PI, collaborators, and other researchers, their qualifications, productivity, and ability to carry out the proposed work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers' comments: 'Strong investigator with substantial publications dealing with this and similar organisms'; 'Highly experienced... perfectly positioned to carry out the proposed work'; 'Extremely well qualified scientists.' Strengths include appropriate collaborators and access to required expertise and labelled organisms. Numeric example scores in critiques: 1–2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine whether the application challenges and seeks to shift current research or clinical practice paradigms, employs novel theoretical concepts, approaches or methodologies, or addresses an innovative hypothesis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers' comments emphasize novelty: 'Enteric infection has not been studied with this organism'; 'Looking at an emerging pathogen through a new lens.' Strength/qualification: topic is novel though some experiments are descriptive; one reviewer notes descriptive nature may limit perceived innovation. Numeric example scores in critiques: 2–3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the overall strategy, methodology, analyses, potential problems, alternative strategies, and benchmarks for success; consider whether the approach is well-reasoned, feasible, and appropriate to accomplish the aims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers' comments: 'Entirely straightforward analysis of the mode of pathogenesis on an enteric infection'; 'Use of RFP/GFP labeled organisms should be useful to follow'; 'Use of CD18 null mice may (or may not) provide real insights'; 'A first experiment to screen different clinical isolates for oral infectivity is feasible.' Weaknesses/concerns: 'Uses lots of different genetic backgrounds - may be more useful to figure out what is going on in the C57Bl6'; 'Including the avirulent B. thailandensis... could provide a valuable negative control'; 'Although the enteric link could be coincidental, studies should be done to detect where the reservoir of bacterial is in infected host.' Numeric example scores in critiques: 1–2. Emphasis on feasibility, controls, choice of strains/backgrounds, and clarity of mechanistic insight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider whether the scientific environment in which the work will be done contributes to the probability of success, institutional support, equipment, and other resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers' comments: 'Outstanding group at Ft. Collins with documented expertise and publications using their BSL3 facility'; 'RBL facilities are exceptionally good for BSL3 work'; 'Satisfactory.' Strengths highlight excellent BSL3 facilities, institutional support, and collaborator expertise. Numeric example scores in critiques: 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact / Impact/Priority
rubrics_metrics.description: An overall impact score reflecting the reviewers' assessment of the likelihood that the project will exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research field(s) involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narrative guidance from the summary: 'This well reasoned and supported application has the potential to change the way we think about melioidosis... very high level of enthusiasm.' Strengths that drive impact include strong preliminary data, accomplished investigator and team, logical set of experiments, and potential for paradigm-shifting insights. (Note: Impact/Priority score field shown but not filled in this document.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of protections for human subjects when applicable, including risks, protections, benefits, and importance of knowledge to be gained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this application: 'Not Applicable (No Human Subjects)'. Reviewers must state applicability and, when applicable, evaluate appropriateness of protections and compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the involvement of vertebrate animals, justification, and the adequacy of procedures to minimize discomfort, distress, and pain, and compliance with relevant policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document statements: '30-Vertebrate animals involved - no SRG concerns noted'; multiple critiques list 'Acceptable' and 'Mice will be used as the host and handled humanely.' Reviewers check acceptability of vertebrate animal use and humane treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazards
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the proposed research involves biohazards and whether appropriate containment, facilities, and procedures are in place to protect personnel and the environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This application: listed as 'Acceptable' (and in one critique 'Not Applicable (No Biohazards)'). Reviewers note BSL3 facility expertise as strength. Ensure biohazard protections are adequate and documented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select Agents
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether work involves Select Agents and whether the applicant meets biosafety and regulatory requirements for handling them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This application: 'Acceptable'. Reviewers indicate acceptability when regulatory and safety requirements are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate plans for sharing data, model organisms, and other resources as applicable to enable broad distribution and reuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document status in this application: 'Not Applicable (No Relevant Resources)' and elsewhere 'Acceptable'. Reviewers note when plans are not relevant or when they meet expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Period of Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider whether the requested budget is reasonable, appropriate for the proposed research, and whether the period of support is justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative note: 'The budget shown is the requested budget and has not been adjusted to reflect any recommendations made by reviewers.' Committee recommendation here: 'Recommend as Requested' / 'The budget was recommended as requested.' Reviewers may recommend funding level but final calculation is institute grants management staff responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee Resume / Summary Considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Concise synthesis of committee discussion highlighting the principal reasons for strengths, weaknesses, and the committee's overall impression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example language used to summarize reviewer rationale: 'The panel is genuinely excited by the work proposed and there is a very high level of enthusiasm.' Strengths consolidated include accomplished investigator/team, strong preliminary data, doable experiments, logical approach, and potential paradigm-shifting insights. These resume comments communicate how reviewers weighed criteria in aggregate.
